findings.title: User verification skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet
findings.body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises DoesNotExist, the view calls `pipeline.next_step()` without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installer. The Integration row only exists once the installation webhook has been processed. So if an attacker finishes the pipeline with someone else's `installation_id` before that webhook lands (or if it is delayed or dropped), no ownership check runs at all. `build_integration` then binds that installation to the attacker's Sentry org. The sender check needs to apply on this path too, for example by verifying installer ownership via the GitHub API.

findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks `sender`
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every Integration has a `sender` entry. `build_integration` only sets it when `state.get("sender")` is present, and older or otherwise-created integrations won't have it. For an orphaned Integration without `sender` (no OrganizationIntegration), this raises KeyError and the user gets a 500 instead of the error page. Use `.get()` and render the error page when the key is missing.

findings.title: Unhandled exceptions from token exchange / user lookup
findings.body: `get_user_info` raises `GitHubApiError` on a non-2xx response from `/user`, for example a revoked token or a rate limit. `safe_urlopen` can also raise on network errors, and it is called outside the try block. None of these are caught, so the user gets a 500 instead of the documented 'Invalid installation request' page. Wrap both calls and return `error(...)` on failure.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL query parameters not URL-encoded
findings.body: `redirect_uri` is an absolute URL containing `:` and `/` characters, and `client_id` and `state` are interpolated directly into the query string without encoding. If any value contains `&`, `#` or `?`, the authorize URL is malformed. Build the query with `urlencode`.

findings.title: Reinstall of a non-ACTIVE existing Integration now always fails
findings.body: Before this change, an Integration with no OrganizationIntegration was allowed to proceed whatever its status. Now the lookup filters on `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE`, so a disabled or pending-deletion Integration row hits the generic 'Invalid installation request' error. Users can then no longer re-install that GitHub installation, and the error message is misleading.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the 404 path
findings.body: The test now sends a deliberately wrong `state` (`ddd023...`), so it fails at the state-mismatch check and asserts 'Invalid installation request.'. The `/app/installations/{id}` 404 handling in `build_integration` ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') is never reached. That behaviour has lost its coverage, and the state-mismatch case is tested only by accident.
